page: Amazon Web Services i3en.6xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The compute layer is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, offering 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory capacity sits at 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, giving an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not include a GPU, but comes integrated with 15,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward multi-threaded parallel throughput and large dataset access rather than peak single-core speed. PassMark CPU score (20,289.31) and multi-core stress-ng (20,294.6) both register in the middle 50% percentile, while single-thread stress-ng (1,284.79) and Geekbench single-core (1,041.0) sit in the lower 25%. In-memory execution delivers consistent middle-tier throughput, demonstrated by 19.46 million Redis SET operations per second and 106.0 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Instruction set support includes AVX and AVX-512F, with missing extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI limiting heavier machine learning inference tasks, as reflected in lower prompt processing rates on 7B LLM models.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the i3en.6xlarge offers high value where extreme local storage capacity and memory density are required simultaneously. The tradeoff lies in its moderate per-thread compute performance, making it inefficient for CPU-bound serial execution. It fits distributed databases, NoSQL clusters, search indexing engines, big data analytics, and large distributed file systems needing immediate access to 15 TB of local fast storage.
